key_insight: In sloping ocean bottom boundary layers, baroclinic shear can lower the minimum internal-wave frequency enough for near-inertial waves to undergo parametric subharmonic instability (PSI), transferring wave energy into small-scale turbulence and mixing.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a plausible near-bottom mixing mechanism that matters for predicting boundary-layer turbulence, tracer transport, and parameterizations over sloping topography.
method: Linear stability analysis of PSI in a baroclinic bottom boundary layer
Nonlinear simulations to test growth rates and energy pathways
Assessment of how stratification and slope Burger number control instability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement between linear stability theory and nonlinear simulations, showing PSI growth depends on vertical stratification and slope Burger number and that wave shear production is the dominant energy source.
watch_item: The instability appears sensitive to local stratification, bottom slope, and flow state, so it may only occur in specific near-bottom conditions rather than as a universal mixing mechanism.
paper_title: Parametric Subharmonic Instability in the Ocean Bottom Boundary Layer
